html:
After they took power again in 2021, the Taliban barred Afghan girls from secondary school. Afghanistan became the only country in the world where girls may not study beyond primary school.

In September 2021 secondary schools reopened for boys only. In March 2022 the Taliban were expected to let girls back, but they reversed the decision on the morning schools were due to open. In December 2022 they banned women from universities and from working for aid groups, and later from many other jobs, from parks and gyms, and from travelling far without a male relative.

The Taliban had done much the same in their first rule, from 1996 to 2001. The decisions come from their supreme leader, Hibatullah Akhundzada, and his circle in Kandahar, against the wishes of some Taliban officials. The United Nations has called the system gender apartheid. It marks a sharp reversal for a country whose constitution of 1964 had given women the vote, and the ban is one of the main reasons most governments have refused to recognise the Taliban since the fall of Kabul.
sum: After they took power again in 2021, the Taliban barred Afghan girls from secondary school. Afghanistan became the only country in the world where girls may not study beyond primary school.
